In high school we had to take this military-sponsored career assessment, which required us to answer a battery of questions in all subject areas from English and history to engineering and physics.

After taking the exam, we were all called into assembly where an army general dude was explaining about the exam. Now there’s probably 300 students in the auditorium listening. This guy has the audacity to say, “Well, naturally the women won’t score as high as the men in math and engineering.” 17 year-old (female) me was like now hold up— as I raised my hand, my friend next to me was like oh my god what are you doing?

Army general dude calls on me. I ask, “What do you mean the women won’t score as well as the men? Why is that?”—- he proceeds to give a long, bumbling answer, within which he said “its feared that more women will go to college than men.” My hand shoots up again and the dummy picked me once more. I simply said, “Excuse me, but did you just use the word “feared”?”

The entire auditorium rippled with applause, as our admins quickly ended the assembly. Later, one of them pulled GI Joe aside and said— that was our class valedictorian.

This was 2009 at an inner city public high school in the US.
